fact: The boot now asks its own routes for content, not only for an answer. Nine paths are checked for a string the branch behind them cannot produce without having run -- the LCARS title, native-ternary, exact-full-corpus, the tercode cross-check reporting identical:true, and the packed-alphabet divergence labelled rather than hidden -- with the needles measured off the running platform instead of declared. The image that booted reports: 'init: 19 of the routes asked answered -- the platform is up; 9 of them returned the content they exist to return', with zero CONTENT failures and 'DASHBOARD: http://127.0.0.1:5183/ui/ on this machine, and http://10.0.2.15:5183/ui/ over the network (eth0 is linked)'. The check found two defects on its first runs, both in itself: http_req NUL-terminated the response at the status line so the status could print, and the content check then searched that same buffer -- it reported all nine routes as answering without their content; moved out of the retry loop and pointed past the header terminator, it agreed. The first version also printed every body ten times over an 11 KB/s serial line (350 KB of console for one boot), so the content probes are silent unless they fail and the same boot now writes 94109 B.
not_claimed: Content assertions are checks the platform answers about itself. They prove the ternary branch ran and the dashboard is the LCARS page; they do not prove an association, and they are not a functional test of what the routes return -- a route that returned a wrong ranking with the right field names would pass.
